chunks: What was narrated by Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Faḍḍāl, from some of our companions, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
"The sunnah (prophetic tradition) in the salat (prayer) of the day is with low recitation, and the sunnah (prophetic tradition) in the salat (prayer) of the night is with audible recitation."

key_terms.اَلسُّنَّةُ: the established sunnah (prophetic tradition) or normative prescribed practice

ai.seo_question: Should recitation in daytime and nighttime salat (prayer) be quiet or audible?
ai.summary: This hadith states the sunnah (prophetic tradition) regarding recitation in salat (prayer): daytime prayers are recited quietly, while nighttime prayers are recited audibly. It conveys a practical legal ruling in the manner and description of ritual prayer.
